_comment: Public claims motif makes, each with a verdict and reproducible evidence. Populated by reading the shipped surfaces, not by generating from source. A checker reads this file; see the drift-check work that follows.

_inclusionRule.summary: A span of shipped text is a claim when all three tests pass. Written before the inventory so the boundary is reviewable rather than decided per entry.
tests: Ships to a reader. README, the landing components under apps/docs/theme/landing, docs content under apps/docs/content, and package.json descriptions. Source comments, tests, and workspace-only files are not shipped text.
Asserts something about motif, or grades another library. A capability, a number, a comparison, a guarantee. Grading a competitor counts, because it is a claim about that competitor.
A reader could act on it. Choosing motif, expecting a capability to exist, or believing a competitor lacks one.
excluded: Install and usage instructions, and code samples that only demonstrate the API. 'npm install usemotif' asserts nothing.
API reference prose that describes a signature or a default. The types are the gate for those, not this ledger.
Text already marked as forthcoming or roadmap at the point of reading. Recorded only if the marking is absent or easy to miss.
_inclusionRule.includedEvenWhenSoft: A claim a reader relies on but nobody could falsify still gets an entry, verdicted 'unfalsifiable'. Leaving it out would hide the softest and most load-bearing marketing.

worked.why: Fails test 2. An instruction, not an assertion.

worked.text: A thin factory. The returned object is exactly the input - `createTheme` does no transformation
worked.why: Fails the API-reference exclusion. It describes a signature's behaviour, and the type system plus the unit tests already gate it.

worked.text: Every unique style bag becomes one CSS rule.
worked.why: Passes all three. It asserts a specific emission behaviour, and a reader sizing up runtime cost would act on it. Note it is also the sentence that contradicts the 'atomic CSS' label used elsewhere.

_verdicts.holds: True, and the evidence proves it. Leave the copy alone.
_verdicts.fails: False as written. Retire or rewrite.
_verdicts.qualify: True under a condition the copy omits. Add the condition.
_verdicts.unfalsifiable: Marketing with no testable content. A judgement call, not a defect.
_verdicts.unresolved: Could not be settled with the evidence available. Escalate; never silently keep.

_evidenceKinds.source: A path, optionally a symbol, that must exist and say what the entry claims it says.
_evidenceKinds.command: A command that must exit zero.
_evidenceKinds.artifact: A value in a tracked gate file. Name what to check with `field` (a dotted path into the JSON, quoting a segment that contains a dot) plus the `value` it must equal, or with `symbol` for a substring. A path alone proves only that the file exists, which is a citation rather than evidence: the check reports those separately every run.
_evidenceKinds.manual: A person verified it. A checker reports these rather than passing them, because they are the ones that drift silently.
_evidenceKinds.doc: A cited URL on the graded library's own documentation, with the quoted statement in the note. Required for any claim about a library this project does not control.

_locating: `text` is the claim as it was written when the inventory ran, and it never changes. `line` is advisory: lines move whenever anything above them is edited, so a checker searches for `text` within `file` and treats a moved line as a hint to update, not a failure. An entry with a `disposition` has been answered, and its `text` is deliberately no longer in the file; check `disposition.now` instead. An entry with no `disposition` whose `text` has vanished is the real failure: the copy moved and nobody recorded why.

_coverage.landing: All 15 files under apps/docs/theme/landing read. 8 carry entries, 7 are claim-free.

docs.screenMethod: Every page matched against a claim-signal pattern: competitor names, superlatives and comparatives, zero-cost phrasing, multipliers, and figures with KB, MB, or ms units.
docs.note: 21 pages signalled and all 21 were read. Only guides/performance.mdx carries claims under the inclusion rule; the other 20 signals were false positives, mostly prose about CI lanes, render props, or a style bag having no runtime dependencies. The 169 pages that produced no signal were screened, not read in full. They are recorded as screened rather than claim-free, because an empty pattern result is weaker evidence than a reading.

themes: The atomic-CSS label is wrong in five places and is the single most repeated defect. The runtime emits one class per style bag, hashed and deduped. The docs describe that correctly at guides/performance.mdx line 27, so this is a label that drifted from the project's own prose, not a disagreement about the code.
Three version-shaped claims are stale: the README says the scope ships at 1.0.0, the stats strip says stable since 1.1, and the landing changelog presents 1.0.2 as recent. The tree is at 1.4.0.

The published benchmark multiples were never updated after the baselines were refreshed. They read two to three times the current gate floors, because they were measured against a competitor version the old pin could never reach.

Twenty-four gradings of other libraries carry no recorded basis. One is demonstrably wrong: styled-components is graded as having no React Native support, and it ships a documented native entry point.

Where a claim spans platforms or rendering models, the copy tends to state the web case unconditionally. SSR and RSC are graded as one cell; token resolution is described as having no context read, which is exactly what native does.
judgementCalls: The comparison set is styled-components, vanilla-extract, and CSS Modules, all web-only, while the project's own plan names Tamagui and NativeWind as what a primary user would otherwise reach for.
The testimonials are invented quote bodies, disclosed as illustrative in the section framing.
The bento performance chart shows motif at 20 percent against five unlabelled competitors, with no data source.
_report.note: Verdicts are arguments. Each entry's evidence field is there so a specific one can be disagreed with rather than the whole ledger accepted or rejected.
